question: Does training-time context-enriched (same-passage subgraph) triple/path supervision already exist and subsume the proposed method, or is context injection predominantly an inference-time/prompting technique?
description: The core novelty claim is that context should enrich the training supervision signal, not only inference-time retrieval. If prior work already fine-tunes on subgraphs or passage-grounded supervision, the contribution shrinks to an empirical comparison.
rationale: Retrieved work so far (SG-RAG MOT doi:10.20944/preprints202505.1992.v1; KICGPT doi:10.18653/v1/2023.findings-emnlp.580; GreaseLM/MHGRN doi:10.18653/v1/2020.emnlp-main.99) injects subgraphs/KG context at retrieval or inference time; none was found that isolates same-passage context as a training-time supervision variable.
resolution: Partially resolved by the retrieved set: no directly matching work was found that uses same-passage context triples as a training-time supervision signal. All analyzed context-construction works (SG-RAG MOT, CLAUSE, Co-E, the answer-path prompt study) manipulate context at inference for an un-retrained reader, and the training-time works found (EmbedKGQA, GreaseLM, Variational Reasoning, STRuCT-LLM) do not use passage-context supervision. This is a search result over the recorded queries only; alternative terminology (e.g., contextualized KG pretraining, passage-grounded instruction tuning, graph-augmented LM pretraining) has not yet been searched.
